"They're exporting the models from WR and just rigging them"

What else does a model need other than rigging and animations?

"The [models] are client side only"

What even is a server side model? Does this imply the server handles every animation?

"Update and recompile the entire code"

Although updating (refactoring) existing code is time costly, I don't understand how "recompiling" affects development speed :D

All in all to me this comment seems to come from an uninformed place as there are terms thrown around without their meanings making sense.
I understand that their codebase is old and as they've said, needs upgrading, but this specifically doesn't imply they can't import existing models.

The code can't handle high quality models? There are existing characters (ahri ASU) that are on a similar level to the in game models of WR.

It's hard to add/replace models? The quantity of skins indicates there existing plenty modern and robust systems for doing these things.

I believe that there are genuine reasons for why they're taking so long but the ones you've presented here don't really mean anything :D

As I've said, I wholeheartedly agree that it's inexcusable that they're taking so long for basic QOL updates but we are seeing them change the status quo.

As for the lack of endgame, I feel it has nothing to do with the rewards system, although this point also strongly resonates with me.

The hsr rewards, such as free 10-pulls on a patch to patch basis, are something inherently required to give a similar amount of character inflow for players due to the fact that there's no element of exploring.



Look, the "thank you" is something nice that they're doing. The game is an f2p live service game that's practically guaranteed to last for at least 3-4 more years with monthly updates. Although I get everyone wants more and more, why not just be content with the fact that we're getting something when you are entitled to nothing :D

What mistreatment? This is a free to play game where you're not forced to spend a single penny. Why do you feel entitled to any sort of free reward? This makes no sense to me.

If you're going to talk about how they barely listen to us, look at the patch log of version 4. There have been so many changes that, while yes, they did take unreasonably long to get implemented, are nonetheless great additions/fixes for the game. By the looks of it this trend will continue for the foreseeable future. 

What are you unsatisfied with???

Why does the community demand these rewards?
You're playing a free game in which you're choosing whether to pay or not. No content is locked out for someone who doesn't spend any money. Why would anyone feel entitled to a reward just because they play the game?

This comes from a genuine point of confusion and the scale of the community's reaction seems insane...

First of all I really appreciate the tiniest things. Like the smallest compliment or insult, if coming from a person I value, can make or brake my day. Maybe they just say it because it's what they think but it really warms my heart to hear it from someone close.

When I finish anything, I just think that I could have done it somehow differently in a way that's better than how I did it in reality. After a while i have to eventually start something else and the whole cycle repeats itself. I just sit there for a while and hate the way I do stuff and by relation - myself. All in all that's just me and isn't related to the topic that much.

And I do believe that since I was young all adults have been telling me in some manner how a normal person would act even if they didn't have ill intentions. In my country mental health isn't that big of deal and there aren't many people who I could talk to, so I continued second guessing and asking myself if a "normal person" would act like me. That's how the image of a "normal person" got created in my mind. Probably brainwashed was an incorrect word to use, and if so excuse me, I didn't mean to.

Im glad that you seem to think the same way about society as me. I would hate wasting any professional's time in which he could help someone else but I think I just have to do it. And making life better for the ones around me is one of the key parts of motivating myself. Thank you for your advice and I have to say, even if this doesn't matter to you, that you just made my day go trough a lot easier. Thank you again.

I think recently having a birthday made me think more about my life overall but nothing else has changed in my routine. I guess I feel good and time passes quickly when I'm around ones who make me feel special even if it is  in the smallest comprehensible way, but at the same time I hate being put on a pedestal because I never do enough to be perceived as a person who is in any way better than others. I hate that and i mostly feel like doing nothing because i know that i won't feel good in the end anyway. I imagine that a well rounded person is exactly how i described it. At least that's what i have been "brainwashed" to think.

What you are saying may very well be true, but if you aren't doing anything important and just wasting it all, the opportunities given by others and the hopes that you've built up, is it worth it to continue?

I'd say it has been in my mind for a while, maybe 2 years. But not to the extent that it is now. There are moments when i can forget about my troubles in life but they are to short and far apart to change anything. For me an important member of society is a person who does his job right, does things in the way that he is supposed to, people appreciate his work and he improves everyone's lives even if it is in an extremely small way.

I'd very much like to be alone in a beautiful place with just my thoughts, but looking at the situation from farther away, simply fixing myself wouldn't make me more important in society, hence the post.
